cases.notes: The X-Signature request header (not the body field the HMAC is computed over) is the attacker-controlled input this CWE-347 case concerns: the vulnerable twin recomputes the HMAC and compares it to this header's value with PHP's `==` operator, vulnerable to a "magic hash" type-juggling collision. Modeled on a real Slack-style Events-API callback receiver (docs/research/category3-saas-functionality-and-cwe-research.md sec 1/6a). Served at its own illustrative per-cell URL (served_url_for(), not the shared manifest route.path `/webhooks/events`, since Huddle Hub has no migrated real page to anchor a pinned URL to). LABGEN-HHB-0001 in lab/manifests/webhook_signature_huddlehub_sample.yaml, CC-LAB-0133/FR-LAB-115 -- never a PFF-* case.

The pasted url is fetched server-side with zero validation of its host/scheme -- real SSRF, CWE-918. Modeled on a real Slack-style "link unfurling" feature (docs/research/category3-saas-functionality-and-cwe-research.md sec 2/6a). Served at its own illustrative per-cell URL, same reasoning as HHUB-0001. LABGEN-HHB-0003 in lab/manifests/ssrf_huddlehub_sample.yaml, CC-LAB-0134/FR-LAB-116 -- never a PFF-* case.

triggerWord is concatenated directly into a raw outbound HTTP request header block for a webhook-delivery POST -- an embedded CRLF splices in an arbitrary extra header the destination receives, CWE-93. Modeled on a real Slack-style outgoing-webhook delivery feature (docs/research/category3-saas-functionality-and-cwe-research.md sec 1/6a). Served at its own illustrative per-cell URL, same reasoning as HHUB-0001. LABGEN-HHB-0005 in lab/manifests/header_injection_huddlehub_sample.yaml, CC-LAB-0135/FR-LAB-107 -- never a PFF-* case.
